blogs.title: Fair Use on the Fast Track: Santos v. Kimmel and the Rule 12(b)(6) Doctrine
blogs.description: Delve into how the Second Circuit applied the four‑factor fair‑use test at the pleading stage to dismiss a set of user‑generated videos. The post explains what the court deemed “transformative” in the context of late‑night satire, how it weighed market harm, and why this decision provides a clearer roadmap for comedic creators facing early procedural denials.

blogs.title: The Lost Loss: Why Santos’s Fraudulent Inducement Claim Failed
blogs.description: Examine the New York prerequisite that a fraudulent inducement claim must allege a specific out‑of‑pocket loss. The article breaks down the court’s reasoning in rejecting Santos’s allegation and discusses the broader implications for future litigation involving fan‑based defrauding accusations.

blogs.title: When Copyright Blocks State Law: The Preemption of Santos’s Breach Claims
blogs.description: Explore how the U.S. Copyright Act preempts state‑law breach‑of‑contract claims when they arise from the same underlying act of alleged infringement. The piece unpacks the court’s application of the preemption doctrine and clarifies the hard line that bars claims like Santos’s despite their facially distinct content.

blogs.title: Good Faith, Bad Faith, and the Fair‑Use Shield: Santos v. Kimmel’s Bad‑Faith Argument
blogs.description: Analyze the court’s dismissal of Santos’s claim that Kimmel’s false representations invalidate a fair‑use defense. Drawing on Harper & Row and subsequent jurisprudence, the post discusses how the court balanced the presumption of good faith with the realities of satirical commentary and the broader consequences for content that relies on fictional personas.
